answer.allocation: Both cells are 0x30-byte, align-8 Arc allocations; the cell pointer sits at closure +0x20 in both families (closure sizes differ: X4 entry size 0x30, X5 0x48). Size pinned by the spawn alloc immediate (0x30), the 0x30-byte stack image copied into the allocation, and the cell glue dealloc immediate (0x30).
answer.family_differences: Layout offsets are identical across type-A, X4 and X5.  The families differ as monomorphisations (own cell glue, payload drop and context-release glue per family, over distinct context object types) and in two uses: the X5 finish store takes its vtable half from closure +0x30 where X4 (and type-A) take the entry base in r15; and X5 has a join body that takes the pair out, while no body takes the X4 pair.

fields.consumers: incremented for the closure/package copies at spawn; decremented by the dispatcher after its finish store, by the join body (X5), by handle drops and caller releases (#3148); the cell glue runs when a decrement reaches zero
fields.name: strong_count

fields.consumers: CAS sentinel of the X5 join take (1 -> -1, restored to 1; #3074 semantics); decremented by the cell glue before the 0x30-byte dealloc
fields.name: weak_count

fields.consumers: payload drop bookkeeping (flag byte at A+0x20 on a discarded live pair, decrement of the counter at A+0x18, xchg on the word at [A+0x10]+0x28); released by the cell glue through the family context-release slot
fields.name: context_pointer
fields.producer: spawn body, from its r9 argument (saved at spawn entry, copied into the cell image); the spawn body increments the counter at A+0x18

fields.consumers: dispatcher pre-store drain test; payload drop (drains, then zeroes the word); cell glue re-test (unwind paths, via the family drain helper on the triple at +0x18); X5 join (bit 0 test, word cleared on take)
fields.name: state
fields.producer: spawn body writes 0; only the dispatcher finish block writes 1 (fall-through and landing-pad copies)

fields.consumers: X5 join take (loaded out); drained (dropped + deallocated through the stored vtable) by the dispatcher, the payload drop, the cell glue and the drain helper. X4: drained only, never taken
fields.name: data
fields.producer: dispatcher finish block only; the spawn pair slot is uninitialised. Normal path: 0 (r14 zeroed at dispatcher entry). Catch path: the panic Box data pointer from the catch-pair helper (slot 0x64dfe88)

fields.consumers: same readers as data; the drain paths call [vtable] as the drop fn and read size at [vtable+0x08] and align at [vtable+0x10]
fields.name: vtable
fields.producer: dispatcher finish block only. Normal path, X4: r15 = the entry base 0x64c5330, loaded by the thread start routine from package +0x10 (#3050). Normal path, X5: r15 = the word at closure +0x30, the vtable half of the closure environment fat-pointer field at closure +0x28, copied by the spawn body from its caller argument struct; the dispatcher loads r15 from closure +0x30 at entry. Catch path: the panic Box vtable from the catch-pair helper

boundaries.adapter_semantics: What the two adapters per dispatcher do with their environment copies (X4 slots 0x64ecb60/0x64ecb58, X5 slots 0x64ecb98/0x64ecb88) is not revisited; neither adapter receives the cell pointer, and neither performs the completion store.
boundaries.context_identity: What the context object A at cell +0x10 is at source level is not pinned for either family (same limit as #3050 for type-A): the binary shows a refcounted object (counter at A+0x18 incremented by the spawn bodies, flag byte at A+0x20, a related object pointer at A+0x10 whose +0x28 word the payload drop xchgs) handed to each spawn body as argument r9; no string or Location names it on these paths.
boundaries.drain_reachability: Whether the dispatchers' pre-store drain (and the glue drain) ever sees a live pair is a run-time question: each dispatcher runs once per fresh cell whose state starts at 0, and static analysis does not decide how a second store into the same cell would arise.  Only the drain paths and the offsets they use are pinned.
boundaries.join_x5_semantics: The take/release semantics of the X5 join body 0x5cf7550 (CAS protocol, reference release order, diagnostics) are the subject of open PR #3074 (RE-012) and are not re-derived here; this packet pins only the cell offsets that body reads and writes, as one consumer of the layout.
boundaries.x5_env_pair_identity: What the fat-pointer field at X5 closure +0x28/+0x30 is at source level is not pinned: the spawn body copies both words from its caller argument struct into the closure image, the dispatcher passes the pair to its second adapter and stores only the +0x30 word into a finished cell.  Its data word is discarded on the finish path (r14 is zeroed), so the cell never holds that pair itself.

limits: Static analysis only; no captured code was executed. Body boundaries are FDE extents cross-checked by SHA-256.  Producer/consumer closure rests on the byte-pinned bodies above plus the completion-store idiom census of #3050 (13 bodies: the 11 dispatchers and two stack constructions) and the take-idiom census of #3148 (exactly two join bodies), which bound the set of bodies that can store into or take out of any dispatcher packet cell.
question: The packet-cell producers packet (#3050) left the families X4/X5 classified only far enough to exclude them from the type-A cell: they use different cell types (own drop-glue slots 0x64ecb50 / 0x64ecc48), but their cell layouts were not pinned, and the sibling-join packet (#3148) pinned JoinHandle ownership without pinning the cells.  What is the layout of the packet cell the X4 dispatcher 0x5cd9b30 and the X5 dispatcher 0x5cf7710 drain -- allocation size, field offsets, and the producer and consumer of each field?
